did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with the prophetic formula, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,” indicating that the message that follows is presented as the word of the LORD to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel asks about the vine: How is a vine branch better than the trees of the forest? This question introduces the parable about the vine’s uselessness as building material.
The prophet emphasizes that a vine branch is unsuitable for making anything—not even a peg on which to hang a vessel.
The vine is portrayed as material handed over to the fire: both ends have been consumed by fire, and its middle has been scorched. The question is therefore whether it can still be used for anything.
Even when the vine was whole, it was not considered suitable for making anything—how much less after the fire has consumed and scorched it.
Here the meaning of the parable is stated explicitly: Just as the vine is handed over to the fire, so the inhabitants of Jerusalem have been given over.
The image describes a vine that has come out of the fire, yet the fire will still consume it. This emphasizes that the danger and judgment do not end when it escapes the fire.
The stated result is that the land will be made desolate, because its inhabitants have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord GOD.
